subject: Renewal + mid-year top-up: aligning pricing and co-term options
messages:
From: Sarah Klein <sarah.klein@starlite.ai>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@starlite.ai>
Date: 2025-12-04T15:22:00-08:00
Subject: Renewal + mid-year top-up conversation

Hi Neha,

Hope you’re well — we’re in the middle of planning our cloud spend for H1 and have a sharp increase in inference volume projected for Jan–Mar due to a new pilot. We’re approaching our renewal window in Feb and wanted to understand options for: a) a one-time mid-cycle uplift to cover the pilot, b) co-terming the uplift with our Feb renewal, and c) what discount / packaging tradeoffs are available if we commit to a larger reserved bucket.

Attached is a short requirements doc with expected peak TPS and token growth (starlite_requirements_DEC2025.pdf). High level ask: can Redwood provide pricing scenarios (incremental commitment sizes and effective discounts) and indicate what lead time is needed to guarantee capacity? Also need ballpark on how co-terming would affect proration on our Feb invoice.

Would appreciate a quick written set of options to share with procurement, or a 30-min call tomorrow if that’s easier.

Thanks —
Sarah Klein
Head of Platform
Starlite AI
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: Sarah Klein <sarah.klein@starlite.ai>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.com, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@starlite.ai>
Date: 2025-12-04T17:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + mid-year top-up conversation

Hi Sarah — thanks for the context and the requirements doc, that’s helpful. I’ve looped in Jordan (pricing) to pull together concrete scenarios. Short answers up front: we can support a mid-cycle uplift and co-term it at renewal; discounts improve materially with a 12-month commit and reserved capacity, and guaranteeing capacity depends on pool availability (we can reserve).

Next steps I propose:
- Jordan to provide 2–3 price scenarios (short-term uplift only, 6-month bridge + co-term, 12-month top-up with reserved capacity).
- I’ll include our standard proration examples so procurement knows invoice timing implications.
- If these look good, we’ll follow with a formal quote (PDF) and a single-sheet amendment for signature.

I’ve attached a preliminary price sketch (redwood_uplift_quote_v1.pdf) — preliminary numbers only, assuming current usage + a 40% pilot spike. Can you confirm the PO contact and desired SLA (standard or enhanced)?

If you’re free tomorrow at 10am PT I’ll set a quick 30-min sync with Jordan.

Best,
Neha Kapoor

Neha / Sarah — moving to pulled numbers based on the requirements doc and the uplift Neha sketched. Quick summary of viable options (rounded):

Option A — Short-term uplift (6 months)
- Additional reserved units: +200k token-units/month
- Effective uplift rate: $0.54 per 1k tokens (list $0.70)
- Discount: ~22% off list for 6-month bridge; billing proration applied from activation date.
- Capacity: can guarantee if reserved 48h before start date (subject to pool availability).

Option B — Co-term + 12-month commitment (recommended for cost predictability)
- Additional reserved units: +150k token-units/month (annualized)
- Effective rate: $0.45 per 1k tokens (list $0.70)
- Discount: ~36% off list (volume & 12-mo commitment)
- Includes preferential scheduling and 99.9% uptime SLA addendum (requires dedicated capacity add-on).

Option C — Ad-hoc top-up (pay-as-you-go)
- No reserved units; metered usage at $0.64 per 1k tokens
- Discount: 8% for pre-paid credit bundles (non-refundable)

Notes: the 36% tier in Option B assumes a minimum annual uplift commitment (we can convert to a voucher model if procurement prefers amortized payments). I’ve attached an internal pricing matrix for finance to confirm threshold behavior (pricing_matrix_20251205.xlsx).

Neha — I left the 20% vs 36% language off until finance confirms discount corridors; Ben, please advise whether we can authorize the 36% highway for an ARR-anchored uplift or if exec approval is required.

Jordan Blake
Pricing Lead, Commercial Ops
jordan_blake@redwood.com
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: Sarah Klein <sarah.klein@starlite.ai>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@starlite.ai>
Date: 2025-12-05T09:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + mid-year top-up conversation

Jordan / Neha — quick finance read:
- We can approve up to 15% off list in standard uplift approvals for mid-cycle adjustments without exec sign-off.
- Anything >15% (i.e., 20%–36%) requires a one-off commercial approval routed to the CRO and finance director; that’s typical for discounts >$100k impact to ARR.
- Voucher/amortization model: finance prefers a voucher tied to invoiced ARR to keep revenue recognition straightforward. We can accommodate staged invoicing for the 12-month commit, but procurement must accept the voucher terms.

I ran a quick table; if Starlite opts for Option B and signs a 12-month uplift at the suggested quantity, the expected revenue impact is material but acceptable — recommend exec sign-off path but willing to present. Attached the matrix for transparency (pricing_matrix_20251205.xlsx).

Ben Carter
Director, Revenue Operations

Thanks all — Sarah / Tom, summarizing the consolidated options and next steps so procurement has one place to work from:  

Option 1 — 6-month uplift (fastest)
- 200k extra token-units/month for 6 months
- Effective rate: $0.54 per 1k tokens (approx 22% off list)
- Proration: invoice prorated from activation date; no co-term mechanics apply
- Use case: short pilot where you don’t want to change long-term commitment

Option 2 — 12-month co-term commit (cost-optimal, recommended if you expect sustained growth)
- 150k token-units/month annualized
- Effective rate: $0.45 per 1k tokens (approx 36% off list)
- Requires voucher/amortization and signed amendment; preferential capacity scheduling included
- Note: >15% discount requires exec approval (Ben noted we can route this immediately)

Option 3 — Pay-as-you-go top-up
- Metered usage, no reserved capacity
- Rate: $0.64 per 1k tokens (8% discount if pre-paid credit bundle)

Attachments: redwood_uplift_quote_v2.pdf (formalized numbers and amendment stub); pricing_matrix_20251205.xlsx (internal for your review). I’ve also linked the HubSpot deal for quick reference: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/8721/RD-2025-0842

Next steps:
1) Please confirm which option procurement prefers and the PO contact and billing cadence.
2) If Option 2 is preferred, confirm willingness to accept voucher/amortization and we’ll immediately route for exec approval.
3) If you want to lock capacity for Jan, we’d need signed amendment + deposit by Dec 12.

I’m happy to hop on the 30-min call at 10am PT today if you want to go through the tradeoffs live — otherwise I’ll stand by for your preference and PO contact.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
